title: "Who is Hiring?" postings stuck near 12-year lows as AI reaches half of all jobs
lede: HN Trends' November tally counts 244 postings in Hacker News' monthly hiring thread, 37% fewer than a year earlier, while AI now appears in just over half of all listings.

points: Every thread since July has had 224 to 255 postings; August's count was the lowest since January 2014.
AI agents appear in 14.8% of postings, ahead of LLMs, and MCP rose from 0.3% to 4.5% in a year.
Python and TypeScript still lead the languages, and Rust has climbed to third, mostly ahead of Go.
Front End roles fell from 27% of postings in early 2022 to 6.6%; Full Stack and Back End also slipped.
Remote, onsite and hybrid shares barely moved, and Junior roles remain rare at about 3%.

points.text: A recently laid-off commenter says startups now post on Greenhouse, Ashby or Lever instead, so the thread may understate demand.
Commenters disagree on what the drop means: HN postings are not the job market, and nobody can say why they fell.
One employer says the thread now draws so many AI-written applications that filtering them, not AI cuts, is the real problem.
Some argue AI lets fewer, cheaper developers do the work, which moves jobs outside the US.
Commenters broadly agree laid-off developers face a hard market, with searches of six months or more now common.
